title: TENSION: Keel's Prime Relayer Multisig runs at 1-of-2 while its own modification rule demands a majority of signers
content:
Two adjacent provisions describe the same multisig incompatibly. A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2: "The Prime Relayer Multisig currently has a 1/2 signing requirement." A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.5: "Keel can change the signers of the Prime Relayer Multisig at any time, so long as there are at least two (2) signers and **at least a majority of signers are required to execute transactions**."

One signature out of two is not a majority of two. The current configuration therefore fails the constraint that governs changes to it — the state is grandfathered in only because the rule is written as a condition on modification rather than as a standing requirement.

The practical exposure is real, not merely textual. At 1-of-2, a single compromised or coerced signer can exercise the full `RELAYER_ROLE` over Keel's Liquidity Layer, with no second party in the path. What contains the damage is everything outside the multisig: on-chain rate limits that bind any relayer, the separate Freezer Multisig, and Sky's parallel Core Operator Relayer.

Two readings are possible and the text does not settle it: either the 1/2 setting is a deliberate operational trade favouring the speed a relayer needs, with the majority rule intended to apply prospectively; or it is an oversight that the next signer change will silently correct, because any modification must satisfy …1.5. Either way it is a discrepancy a reviewer should raise rather than read past.
description: A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2 records a 1/2 signing requirement, yet …1.5 permits signer changes only if at least a majority of signers is required to execute — and 1 of 2 is not a majority.
